_note: STAKK photoreal cut: edit decision list. Read by src/tools/conform.py (bakes graded, retimed 30 fps JPEG sequences into src/footage/<seq>/) and by the page (src/footage/manifest.json). Times: edit seconds (cues.json grid). keys: [t_edit, t_source, speed_in, speed_out]; between keys the source time follows a cubic Hermite with those speeds (so speed ramps are smooth and measured). Source clips are 24 fps, 1080x1912.

seq.why: owner-approved retake b1_smash_v3 (compact, finely ground ball; the original b1 read as «جنه مخ»). One source frame per output frame for the whole shot (1.25x, nearest, no blends): f30 (1.250 s) at 0.00 -> f56 (2.333 s) at 0.867. The press descends through 0.00-0.37 with the ball whole and sharp under it (f30-f41, 12 frames); f41 (1.708 s) is the kiss, the first compressed frame f42 (1.750 s) lands on the smash cue 0.40, f43-f44 flatten it, f45 (1.875 s, 0.50) is the first sharp pressed frame, then the press holds while the steam starts. No blending anywhere: the press's motion-blurred frames (f36-f44) are shown as photographed, never doubled into a ghost rim

owner laughed at b2_lift: the spatula carried the patty on TOP of the blade, lifted backwards. Replaced by the CD-approved b2_sear (Kling 3.0 Turbo): low side-angle macro of a smash patty searing on the black griddle, crispy lacy browned edges, fat sizzling, steam rising through warm amber bokeh, no tools or hands, slow push-in. One source frame per output frame (1.25x, nearest, no blends): f1 (0.042 s) at 0.90 -> f45 (1.875 s) at 2.367, then the hard cut on the 2.40 beat. f0 is a held start frame (f0->f1 differs by 0.4/255) and is skipped. f1-f45 is the window where the steam curls up left of the title and only reaches «سالفة» in the last frames, and the bokeh lights stay left of the words (from ~f50 a thick steam cloud fills the title band; f76-f120 put a bokeh light behind «طبقة»); the lace edges hold their shape frame to frame. nd: a graduated ND (x0.72 in linear light above y 760, clear by y 980) takes the steam and kitchen behind the title down to S01's background density; the white-balance trim (conform.py TRIM) pulls the amber haze toward S01's kitchen

the red stage opens on the empty toasted heel (c1 f0-f7, a locked-off plate with nothing in frame, 0.35x frame-blended) under the heel label; f7 is reached on 3.233 and shown crisp, so no blend ever mixes in the patty (it first appears in f8). The patty drops through the frame one source frame per output frame: f8 (top edge) 3.267, f9 3.300, f10 3.333, f11 (contact, motion-smeared) 3.367

jump f11 -> f18 across the landing: source f12-f16 are the patty sliding and curling into place (an AI wobble with a curled tip, heavy smear) and f17 still ghosts its left edge. f18 = first crisp settled frame on the patty cue 3.40, then 1.25x one-to-one

back to the wide on action (scale cut, same locked shot): the cheddar is still falling (f68), its corner touches the patty f70, the slice slaps down f71 and lies flat on the cheese cue 4.40 (f72, the crown rule: first landed frame on the beat; its flap's last trace is one frame of blur), clean f73, then the melt starts at 1.25x one-to-one (to f86)
half-time: 1.31x punch-in on the same burger's cheddar drip (c1 f100 -> f112 at 0.6x, frame-blended): the drip grows down the patty over the heel

the second patty falls through the frame (c2 f28-f30, real motion smear), touches the cheddar f31 and is down on the patty2 cue 5.90 (f32, «دبل!» pops on that frame), settles f33 (left edge smeared) and is crisp from f34; one source frame per output frame to f38 (6.10)

jump cut (same locked shot) straight onto the second cheddar slumping onto the patty (f66, already below the «دبل!» band), lying down on the cheese2 cue 6.15 (f67 at 6.167), f68 drape, f69 flat. Skips f39-f65 (the double at rest, then the slice falling through the «دبل!» band)

c3 f58 -> c4 f42 on the 6.90 beat (the stack is at rest on both; the rings settle a few px and steam starts): the sauce tip enters the top f43 (6.933), falls one source frame per output frame, touches the onion f57 on the sauce cue 7.40, then a speed ramp (linear acceleration 1.25 -> 7.3x, nearest frames) runs the rest of the pour: the stream thins (f94, the last attached frame, on 7.80), breaks, a last drip falls (f99 on 7.833) and the pool settles (f105 on 7.867). So the 7.90 jump cut to b7 f4 (same burger, same framing: c4 ends on the frame b7 starts from) only skips the pool settling, not the stream (ECD: before, the full stream vanished on that cut)
